# Project Governance 3.0.0-rc.10.5

Context selection can assess larger repositories and use more of their existing documentation.
Native turn-end observations make supported main-model token usage visible before a chat closes.

- Use one 45-second operation clock, including index preparation, with a 55-second managed prompt
  hook. Isolated context selection defaults to 512 calls and 10 MiB; ordinary task consumers retain
  16 calls and 128 KiB. Explicit settings remain authoritative.
- Extract literal shell comments, configuration purpose fields and key names, and Kotlin
  `expect`/`actual` declarations. Refresh older cached facts once and reuse unchanged verified facts.
- Separate path-only reasons and retain bounded examples. Cache verified unchanged oversized blobs
  without treating byte-budget deferrals or transient read failures as permanent omissions.
- Warn when source sharing is approved but passage selection is disabled. Adoption remains explicit;
  this release does not broaden approved paths, enable delegation or change the coding model.
- Collect supported native usage through a neutral Codex `Stop` observer, with `SessionEnd` as
  catch-up. Exact identities and response deduplication preserve attribution; acceptance, unobserved
  reads and unsupported usage remain unknown.
- Default omitted native-worker output retention to 4 MiB. Preserve explicit caps and warn in
  assignment preflight when a small whole-stream allowance may interrupt a review.

Existing projects keep their explicit budgets and enabled questions. Adopt larger allowances and
passage questions deliberately at a verified pause seam. Review the changed managed hook hash in
Codex. Passing qualification does not establish token savings or accepted development outcomes.
